To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a conceptually simple and efficient model, Global Filter Networks (GFNet), for vision that learns long-term dependencies in the frequency space.

(1) we introduce GFNet, a novel architecture that replaces the self- attention layer in vision transformers and CNNs with a 2D Fourier transform and a multiplication with global filters, (2) we demonstrate that GFNet achieves competitive performance on ImageNet and downstream datasets with significantly less computation and memory cost, (3) we demonstrate that our model is robust to adversarial attacks and achieves competitive performance on the ImageNet-A and ImageNet-R datasets

1) GFNet can be an efficient and robust alternative to CNNs and transformers in image classification; 2) GFNet is more efficient than CNNs and transformers with comparable accuracy; 3) GFNet is robust to various types of corruptions.
